body: Hey, what are we supposed to see? I see the exact same result in your StackBlitz under 9.0-rc.2 and 8.3.14, both running View Engine. Also this seems like the expected behavior to me, as the `Date` value is mutated which the `date` pipe doesn't consider, given that it's pure (which means it requires a new `Date` reference for a change to be picked up)

I'm with @JoostK here - the way I understand things is that mutating an internal state of the `Date` object should _not_ trigger change detection.

Note: the stackblitz doesn't run ivy so it actually _confirms_ that view engine is _not_ updating values... 

I'm going to close this issue now based on the above. @sysmat  happy to re-open if you can demonstrate a regression. Thank you!

Ok in doc for date pipe I find:

> To avoid the need to reformat the date on every change-detection cycle, treat the date as an immutable object and change the reference when the pipe needs to run again.

Hmm, I think that docs are misleading in this case as the `date` pipe [is pure](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/c68200cf426a8cd0bc9ff95b4d0140133c28f661/packages/common/src/pipes/date_pipe.ts#L153) and won't deep-check an object when a reference to it isn't change.

rename.to: date pipe documentation is misleading, the date pipe is a pure pipe

Thank you, @ajitsinghkaler. @rockument69 is already doing a rewrite of Pipes in https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/36820. Fyi, @rockument69, see https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/33897#issuecomment-555440953

@kapunahelewong @jbogarthyde @ajitsinghkaler @sysmat : The pipes.md doc in my PR  #[36820](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/36820) does not change because it already describes DatePipe as a pure pipe.

However, the API doc should change, and I defer to @jbogarthyde who might already be in the process of changing it -- if not, Judy, let me know and I can do it.

The API doc for DatePipe has this sentence: "To avoid the need to reformat the date on every change-detection cycle, treat the date as an immutable object and change the reference when the pipe needs to run again." This may be accurate but it is confusing. I propose replacing it with this sentence:

> DatePipe is executed only when it detects a pure change to the input value.
> A pure change is either a change to a primitive input value (such as `String`, `Number`, `Boolean`, or `Symbol`), or a changed object reference (such as `Date`, `Array`, `Function`, or `Object`).
>
